summary: AegisMD is an autonomous, offline-first clinical decision support and health monitoring web platform designed to safeguard astronaut health during long-duration spaceflight missions where real-time communication with Earth is impossible due to light-time latency. Built upon the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) framework, AegisMD enables non-physician crew members to perform guided self-assessments, track vital signs, execute cognitive Psychomotor Vigilance Tests (PVT), and evaluate ocular or dermal scans across four mission habitats (ISS LEO, Deep Space Transit, Lunar Base, and Mars Surface). Using an interactive human anatomy triage map, real-time physiological simulations, and automated countermeasure protocols, AegisMD translates complex biometric telemetry into clear, actionable medical guidance without relying on continuous ground support. This empowers autonomous crews to detect conditions such as Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), radiation spikes, and circadian fatigue early, ensuring crew safety and mission readiness beyond Low Earth Orbit.
details: AegisMD is an autonomous, offline-first clinical decision support and health monitoring platform that integrates multi-system physiological telemetry into a unified mission medical console for spaceflight operations beyond Low Earth Orbit. Designed for crews facing communication delays of up to fourteen minutes or more on missions to the Moon and Mars, the system translates raw biometric vitals into instant Green, Yellow, and Red triage decisions on an interactive human anatomy map while computing an overall Mission Readiness Index. Crews and flight planners can simulate different operational environments across the International Space Station, Deep Space Transit, Lunar Base, and Mars Surface habitats, as well as test acute spaceflight emergencies such as Solar Particle Events, Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), and circadian fatigue. To support non-physician astronauts in conducting independent medical checks, AegisMD includes a Biometric Self-Exam Lab with built-in NASA Human Research Program measurement guides, a Psychomotor Vigilance Test to evaluate cognitive reaction latency prior to high-risk extravehicular activities, and a Visual Diagnostics analyzer for portable ocular ultrasound and post-EVA dermal imaging. The platform also tracks multi-Sol longitudinal health trends, gamifies daily countermeasure adherence such as resistance workouts, hydration, and autonomic breathing exercises, and compresses medical logs into low-bandwidth telemetry packets for asynchronous Deep Space Network uplink. By providing reliable medical autonomy during communication blackouts, AegisMD safeguards Artemis and future Mars explorers while offering an adaptable offline triage workflow for remote rural clinics, maritime vessels, polar expeditions, and disaster response zones on Earth. The application was built as a responsive single-page web platform using React 18, JavaScript, HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and custom inline SVG anatomical visualizations, deployed publicly via Netlify, with generative AI tools utilized to assist with code structuring, synthesizing NASA reference literature, and producing the watermarked voiceover narration for the demonstration video.
